rounds.text: Zodiac Energy Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation relative to its intrinsic worth, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 318 per share against the current market price of Rs 252, offering a 20.7% margin of safety [E28, E29]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the present market price implies a modest 6.8% earnings growth, which sits well below the 10.0% growth assumed in the base case [E30]. The fundamental operating performance remains robust, highlighted by a strong trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 33% [E8] and recent quarterly metrics demonstrating 23% YoY sales growth and 22% YoY net profit growth [E44, E46]. Profitability is also healthy and outperforming sector peers, with an ROCE of 15.3% surpassing the sector median of 13.6% [E6, E56], alongside an impressive ROE of 19.8% [E7]. Additionally, capital expenditure appears to be bearing fruit as capital work-in-progress dropped 71.4% to Rs 2 Cr, signaling that new capacity has come online [E23], which aligns with positive expectations for upcoming quarters [E42] and a high fundamentals results score of 98/100 [E52]. Conceded: the stock is currently lagging the market with a relative-strength rating of 0, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E33, E34], alongside elevated debt-to-equity leverage of 2.08x [E21] and a negative free cash flow of Rs -27 Cr [E19].

Zodiac Energy Ltd carries severe balance sheet and cash flow risks that undermine its headline profitability. Debt to equity has ballooned to 2.08x, meaning total debt exceeds net worth, with borrowings surging from Rs 175 Cr to Rs 243 Cr in a single year [E21, E22]. This aggressive leverage has failed to generate healthy free cash flow, which plunges to a staggering negative Rs -27 Cr as of March 2026 [E19]. Furthermore, operating cash conversion is deeply concerning, with operating cash flow representing only 32% of operating profit [E20]. Market sentiment and institutional positioning reflect these underlying structural strains. The stock is exhibiting extreme weakness, sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range [E5] and trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E33]. Price momentum is absent, evidenced by a 1-year share price return of -43.6% [E35], a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 [E34], and negative institutional money flow [E27]. Promoters have also trimmed their stake by 2.89 percentage points over recent periods [E24]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing sales growth of 33% alongside an ROCE of 15.3% and an ROE of 19.8% [E6, E7, E8].

Conceded: debt-to-equity stands at 2.08x with borrowings rising to Rs 243 Cr, free cash flow is negative at Rs -27 Cr, and operating cash flow is 32% of operating profit [E19, E20, E21, E22]. However, the bear's focus on cash flow obscures the reality of completed capital expenditure, evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress falling by 71.4% to Rs 2 Cr, which indicates that new capacity is coming online [E23]. This deployed capital is already supporting strong fundamental performance, with trailing sales growing at 33% and net profit increasing by 22% year-over-year [E8, E46]. Furthermore, the company achieves an ROCE of 15.3% and an ROE of 19.8%, both outperforming sector medians [E6, E7, E56]. Conceded: the stock trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with negative institutional flow [E27, E33], but dismissing the underlying turnaround based on stale sentiment ignores that results score 98/100 and a reverse DCF implies only a modest 6.8% earnings growth expectation is currently priced in [E30, E52].

Conceded: capital work-in-progress fell by 71.4% to Rs 2 Cr and trailing sales grew at 33% [E8, E23]. However, citing completed capex does not erase the alarming reality that free cash flow sits deep in the red at Rs -27 Cr, while operating cash flows capture a meagre 32% of operating profit [E19, E20]. This severe cash conversion disconnect means the reported net profit growth of 22% [E46] is failing to translate into actual cash entering the business, rendering the expansion dangerously debt-dependent. That heavy reliance on external funding has pushed borrowings up to Rs 243 Cr, leaving the company saddled with a precarious debt-to-equity ratio of 2.08x where debt significantly exceeds total net worth [E21, E22]. While the bull dismisses the terrible technical picture as stale sentiment, the market's severe verdict is underscored by a relative-strength rating of 0, a 43.6% twelve-month share price collapse, and ongoing institutional money outflow [E27, E34, E35].
